tab_landscape: Evaluation practices for graph simulators and LM social simulators. Metric classes are S for snapshot structural, T for text, MT for marginal temporal, D for temporal dependence, L for predictive or likelihood based, and CL for closed loop rollout. Dep. records whether temporal dependence of the generated stream is tested. CL records whether a closed loop test is performed. Every row is explicitly cited.
tab_synthetic: Synthetic validation of the R2O requirements. The reference stream has memory 0.164 and burstiness 0.464.
tab_rrband: Matched real-window reference distributions. Windows contain 10,000 edges. Pairs are matched on the covariates described above, with window reuse capped at three pairs. Values report mean and standard deviation of each real to real discrepancy.
tab_sched: Scheduler control for the memory coefficient. Real streams are passed through the same round quantization used by the generation pipeline before memory is recomputed. $M^{\mathrm{real}}$ is computed on the full real reference window; Table~\ref{tab:complete-configs} reports real $M$ on each cell's matched reference slots and Table~\ref{tab:matched-horizon} at the matched horizon, so the real reference differs slightly across tables.
tab_erep: Evaluation-window sensitivity on \texttt{wikirevision} using GPT-4o-Mini. The representative and inherited initial windows use the same generation and scoring procedures. Inter-event KS here is the jitter arm statistic (timestamp ties spread within the round quantum) and therefore differs from the as scored KS of Table~\ref{tab:complete-configs} for the same runs.
tab_main: Complete results for the 16 preregistered configurations and eight exploratory Qwen3-8B configurations. Degree MMD reports structural error; KS is pooled actor level inter-event KS against matched reference slots (not the global stream KS of Table~\ref{tab:timing-baselines}); $Z_{\mathrm{KS}}$ is the same discrepancy in real reference units; $M$ is the memory coefficient from the deduplicated representation, with the real value in parentheses; $q_{\mathrm{RR}}$ is the empirical real reference tail position. Superscript $s$ marks a short run; $c$ marks a structural evaluation affected by contamination (\texttt{weibo\_daily} L2 excluded; \texttt{weibo\_tech} L2 scored on the archived 8.65k-edge run); $t$ marks the 200 event truncated archive, for which the structural evaluation is unavailable and timing uses matched slots at the available horizon; $e$ marks exploratory Qwen3-8B configurations added after registration (L1 runs stopped at round boundaries, 4,900 to 5,696 events, so 8B L0 and L1 rows are scored at different event counts; see Table~\ref{tab:matched-horizon}).
tab_matched_horizon: Matched-horizon analysis for the exploratory Qwen3-8B configurations. Each L0 stream is truncated to the event count of its paired L1 stream and rescored using the same procedure. KS uses the original generated representation and $M$ uses the deduplicated representation.
tab_baselines: Timing baseline results on the inherited evaluation window. Baselines condition only on the 1,000-edge seed prefix. Baseline values report mean and standard deviation over 20 simulation seeds. Agent configurations are single archived runs scored using the same global stream timing statistics; this global KS differs from the actor level matched slot KS of Table~\ref{tab:complete-configs}. $\rho_1$ is the global stream lag 1 autocorrelation of the generated stream, with the real value in parentheses: mean over seeds for baselines; for agent rows (Qwen3-30B-A3B) the single archived run on the deduplicated stream, with the real value at the cell's matched horizon. $\rho_1$ is a global stream statistic and need not agree with the per actor memory coefficient $M$ of Table~\ref{tab:complete-configs}. Removing tied events or collapsing the stream to distinct timestamps changes the agent values by at most 0.004 (\texttt{analysis/rho1\_tie\_check.csv}), so they do not arise from round batching.
tab_controls: Configuration-level quantities used in the robustness analysis. $n$ is the number of generated events scored. Zero IET is the fraction of actor level inter-event times equal to zero in the generated stream. $\log(T_g/T_r)$ is the log-duration ratio. CC ratio is count conditioned KS divided by original KS. Shape KS is the pooled KS after dividing each actor's inter-event times by the actor's mean interval (rate normalized Rhythm, Proposition~\ref{prop:separation}). Rhythm is the median actor level KS against the matched real continuation.
